reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space with d=dim_R E>0 and f:E->R differentiable everywhere. For every eta,beta,B,ell in R and x0,xp in E assume eta,beta,B>0,ell>=2, actual grad f globally beta-Lipschitz, norm(x0-eta grad f(xp)-xp)<=sqrt(d eta), and64 beta^2(ell d/B+ell^2)<=1/eta^2. Define h=x0-eta grad f(xp), q=(z->h+sqrt(eta)z)_*stdGaussian(E), P=(z->sqrt(eta)z)_*stdGaussian(E), nu=Lebesgue restricted to(0,1] product P. For theta=pi t/2 set S=< (pi/2)(cos(theta)(x-h)-sin(theta)z),grad f(xp)-grad f(h+sin(theta)(x-h)+cos(theta)z) >, and mB(x)=integral min(B,max(-B,S)) dnu(t,z). Set qhat=q.tilted(mB). First define G=(z->x0+sqrt(eta)z)_*stdGaussian(E); then pi=G.tilted(-f), so the tilt follows the pushforward. Set K=min(B^2/(40 beta^2 d eta^2),B/(8 beta eta)) and C=2exp(2B-K). Then pi,qhat are probabilities and pi<<qhat and qhat<<pi. For actual ENNReal RN derivatives R=dpi/dqhat and S=dqhat/dpi, the real functions (R.toReal)^ell and(S.toReal)^ell are Bochner integrable under qhat and pi respectively. Each corresponding real integral minus1 is <=C. The ENNReal lintegrals of R^ell under qhat and S^ell under pi are each <=ofReal(1+C).
